source_text: Igitur, cum venissemus ad apostoli Pauli sententiam [n105] , quam Scripturarum expertibus Traducianus venditare solitus erat, id est: Per unum hominem peccatum intravit in mundum [n106] , ostendi primitus ipsius sermonis testimonio a loci illius adytis Traducianos fuisse summotos, quando Gentium Magister peccati antiquitatem revolvens ad generationis custodiam quasi fortissimum stipatorem finitum numerum collocasset, ut dicens per unum hominem peccatum intrasse in mundum praescriberet nihil se de generatione sensisse, quae nisi per duos non posset exsistere. Atque assignavi distinctum esse inter commixtionem et peccatum parentum, cum diceretur intrasse peccatum quidem in mundum, sed per eum numerum, qui fetibus non poterat convenire. Actumque est sufficienter per totum libellum peccati ibi non naturam indicatam esse, sed formam, quod a praevaricatoribus post secutis imitatione constaret, non generatione susceptum. Verum quia scriptum legimus in Epistula ad Hebraeos de Iudaeis: Ex uno orti sunt et hoc emortuo [n107] , id est de Abraham, superius quoque in eadem epistula de Christo legitur: Qui sanctificat, et sanctificantur ex uno omnes [n108] , ne horum aliquid vel similium, si inveniri poterit, Traducianus arripiat atque argumentetur quidquam de responsione nostra ponderis fuisse discussum, qua affirmavimus ideo dictum esse unum, per quem transierit peccatum, ne generatio sineretur intellegi, cum inventum sit in hac epistula nomine unius generationem indicatam, ideo, inquam, id retractandum putavi. Ut igitur sit intentus lector, admoneo; multiplici enim haec oppositio genere destruetur. Ibi itaque, ubi commemoratio Abrahae fit et Sarra, eius uxor, inseritur; talis est quippe ordo verborum: Fide qui vocatur Abraham oboedivit in locum exire, quem accepturus erat in haereditatem, et exiit nesciens quo iret. Fide demoratus est in terra promissionis tamquam in aliena in casulis habitando cum Isaac et Iacob, cohaeredibus repromissionis eiusdem; exspectabat enim fundamenta habentem civitatem, cuius artifex et conditor Deus. Fide et ipsa Sarra sterilis virtutem in conceptione seminis accepit etiam praeter tempus aetatis, quoniam fidelem credidit esse qui promiserat. Propter quod ab uno orti sunt et hoc emortuo tamquam sidera caeli in multitudine et sicut harena, quae est ad oram maris innumerabilis [n109] . Cum ergo utrumque commemorasset, id est et Abraham et Sarram, eamque dixisset lege senectutis effetam, sed fide virtutem concipiendi seminis accepisse, secure subdidit ab uno ortos tot populos, qui multitudini conferrentur astrorum. Ut ergo copula exponeretur parentum, tam fidelium praedicatio quam rei gestae veritas imperavit; ut autem de ipsis duobus in commendatione propagatae multitudinis non utrumque, sed alterum diceret, ars laudantis admonuit. Volebat quippe ostendere, certa fides quam magna meruisset; dicens virtute Dei excedentem numeros multitudinem propagatam accomodatius ad laudem operis eius esse perpendens, si ex uno eos quam ex duobus diceret procreatos, maxime cum in laudis augmento, quam ultimus sermo cumulabat, nullum esset historiae dispendium, quam supra utriusque personae commemoratione suppleverat.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore when we had come to the sentence of the apostle Paul which the advocate of inherited sin was accustomed to vend to those inexperienced in the Scriptures, that is: Through one human sin entered into the world, I showed first by the testimony of the speech itself that the advocates of inherited sin had been removed from the inner shrines of that place, when the Teacher of the Gentiles, revolving the antiquity of sin, had placed a finite number as a most strong attendant for the custody of generation, so that saying that through one human sin had entered into the world he would prescribe that he had sensed nothing about generation, which unless through two could not exist. And I assigned that a distinction has been made between the mixing and the sin of parents, when it was said that sin indeed entered into the world, but through that number which could not convene with fetuses. And it was acted sufficiently through the whole little book that there not the nature of sin was indicated, but the form, which stood as taken up by later transgressors by imitation, not by generation. But because we read written in the Letter to the Hebrews concerning the Jews: They have arisen from one and this one dead, that is from Abraham, and above also in the same letter it is read concerning Christ: He who sanctifies, and those sanctified, all from one, lest the advocate of inherited sin snatch any of these or of similar things, if it can be found, and argue that something of weight has been shaken from our response, by which we have affirmed that it was said one through whom sin passed, lest generation be allowed to be understood, when in this letter generation has been found indicated by the name of one, for this reason, I say, I thought it should be retraced. That the reader therefore may be intent, I warn; for this opposition will be destroyed by a multiple kind. There therefore, where commemoration of Abraham is made, Sarah also, his wife, is inserted; for such is the order of words: By faith he who is called Abraham obeyed to go out into a place which he was going to receive into inheritance, and he went out not knowing where he was going. By faith he sojourned in the land of promise as in a foreign one, dwelling in huts with Isaac and Jacob, coheirs of the same promise; for he was expecting a city having foundations, whose craftsman and founder is God. By faith also Sarah herself barren received power in the conception of seed even beyond the time of age, since she believed him faithful who had promised. On account of which from one they have arisen, and this one dead, as the stars of heaven in multitude and as the sand which is at the shore of the sea innumerable. When therefore he had commemorated both, that is both Abraham and Sarah, and had said her exhausted by the law of old age, but by faith she had received the power of conceiving seed, he securely added that from one so many peoples had arisen, who would be conferred to the multitude of stars. That therefore the couple of parents be exposed, both the preaching of the faithful and the truth of the thing done commanded; but that of those two themselves in the commendation of the propagated multitude he would say not both but the other, the art of the one praising admonished. For he wanted to show how great things a certain faith had deserved; saying a multitude exceeding numbers had been propagated by the power of God, weighing it more fitting to the praise of his work if he said them procreated from one than from two, especially when in the increase of praise which the last speech was heaping there would be no loss of history, which above he had supplied by the commemoration of each person.

pass_b_english: When we came to the apostle Paul’s statement that the advocate of inherited sin used to peddle to people unfamiliar with Scripture—‘Through one man sin entered the world’ (Romans 5:12; see this work 2.56–57)—I first showed that the wording itself excluded the advocates of inherited sin from the inner meaning of that passage. When the Teacher of the Gentiles traced sin’s antiquity, he placed a definite number as a powerful guard protecting generation. By saying sin entered the world through one man, he expressly indicated that he meant nothing about generation, which cannot occur except through two. I showed that a distinction had been made between parents’ sexual union and their sin: sin was indeed said to have entered the world, but through a number that could not apply to offspring. Throughout the book we argued sufficiently that the passage identifies not sin’s nature but its pattern, adopted by later transgressors through imitation, not generation.

Yet in the Letter to the Hebrews we read concerning the Jews: ‘They sprang from one, and him as good as dead’ (Hebrews 11:12)—that is, from Abraham. Earlier in the same letter, too, we read of Christ: ‘The one who sanctifies and those who are sanctified are all from one’ (Hebrews 2:11). The advocate of inherited sin might seize on one of these texts, or similar ones if any can be found, and argue that it weakens our answer. We said that ‘one’ was used for the person through whom sin passed so as to exclude generation from the meaning, yet in this letter generation is indicated by the mention of ‘one.’ For this reason, I thought the matter should be reconsidered. I urge the reader to pay attention: this objection will be destroyed in several ways.

Where Abraham is mentioned, his wife Sarah is included too. Here is the sequence of the words: ‘By faith the one called Abraham obeyed the call to go out to a place he was to receive as an inheritance, and he went out without knowing where he was going. By faith he lived in the land of promise as in a foreign land, dwelling in tents with Isaac and Jacob, co-heirs of the same promise. For he was waiting for the city that has foundations, whose designer and builder is God. By faith Sarah herself, though barren, received power to conceive seed even beyond the usual age, because she believed the one who promised was faithful. Therefore from one man, and him as good as dead, there sprang descendants as numerous as the stars of heaven and as countless as the sand along the seashore’ (Hebrews 11:8–12).

After mentioning both Abraham and Sarah, and saying that she was past childbearing through old age but received the power to conceive seed by faith, he could confidently add that from one arose so many people, comparable in number to the stars. Both praise of the faithful and the truth of the event required the parents’ union to be described. But the art of praise prompted him, in commending the multitude descended from those two, to name one rather than both. He wanted to show how much steadfast faith had gained. Saying that God’s power had produced a multitude beyond counting, he judged it more fitting to praise God’s work by calling them descendants of one rather than two. This was especially so because the added praise in the final expression caused no loss to historical accuracy: he had already supplied that accuracy by mentioning both persons.

choices.why: Julian's label for teachers of tradux peccati. Keep the polemic name as a description of transmitted sin, not as a theory of the soul's origin.
For Julian, sin requires rational choice; infants lack usus rationis.
